claims.knowledge: Stator field, rotating armature, commutator, brushes and shaft; coil polarity reversal and pulsating DC at the brushes.
claims.scope: Conventional brushed DC machine. Demo is an ideal single uniform-field coil; practical distributed windings reduce ripple.

claims.knowledge: Conductor force I l cross B; motional emf integral of v cross B; commutation keeps motor torque unidirectional; one coil has dead points.
claims.scope: Field orientation and vector direction explicitly defined. Commutation intervals and load current are omitted in the generator drawing.

claims.knowledge: Turn, coil and winding hierarchy; electrical angle = pole pairs times mechanical angle. Simplex lap a=p and simplex wave a=2. Ka=pZ/(2 pi a).
claims.scope: Winding path counts are explicitly restricted to simplex windings; omega in rad/s, flux in Wb per pole.

claims.knowledge: Ea=k omega, Te=k Ia, converted power=Ea Ia=Te omega; signed motor/generator regimes and armature KVL.
claims.scope: Averaged/radial-gap model with fixed flux. Sign convention is stated; regeneration requires a receptive DC source.

claims.knowledge: Separate, shunt, series, compound short-shunt and long-shunt connections; cumulative and differential MMF.
claims.scope: Schematic is motor current convention. Compound field polarity is not implied by an unlabeled winding symbol.

claims.knowledge: Shunt motor It=Ia+If, V=Ea+IaRa; generator IL=Ia−If, Ea=V+IaRa; steady field current V/Rf.
claims.scope: Positive mode-specific current magnitudes, separate from the signed current used in the reversible-mode lab.

claims.knowledge: Unsaturated series motor torque approximately proportional to Ia squared; light-load speed hazard; fixed-flux straight-line model is not generally valid for series excitation.
claims.scope: Primary-source extension to interpret the lecture topology. Saturation changes proportionality. No unsupported contemporary application claims.

claims.knowledge: Fixed-speed open-circuit curve, saturation, residual excitation, correct field connection, field-resistance intersection and critical-resistance tangent; speed changes self-excited field current.
claims.scope: Course graph readings are approximate; no measured numerical curve is invented. Demo uses an explicitly illustrative analytic curve.

claims.knowledge: Armature and field copper losses; converted power versus shaft power; motor and generator efficiency boundaries and rotational losses.
claims.scope: Brush and stray-load losses omitted; rotational loss held constant only as the exercise approximation. Generator arithmetic corrected.

claims.knowledge: Constant-flux torque-speed equation and effects of armature voltage, series resistance, field flux and constant load intersection.
claims.scope: Steady state. Root is a mathematical operating point; current, thermal and mechanical limits must be checked.

claims.knowledge: Approximate constant-torque operation below base speed and constant-power field-weakening operation above base speed.
claims.scope: Fixed current limit, armature voltage limit, negligible resistance drop/loss approximation. Not unlimited field weakening.

claims.knowledge: Full electrical and mechanical differential equations; finite inductance implies continuous current; finite inertia implies continuous speed; starting resistor and fast-current approximations.
claims.scope: The course instantaneous-current answers are explicitly interpreted as La→0 electrical estimates, not exact finite-La switching values.

claims.knowledge: Solution checks: field topology, flux assumption, sign convention, SI units, power boundary, energy balance and operating constraints.
claims.scope: Derived engineering checklist from the cited equations, not an additional empirical claim.

models.title: Ideal rotating coil and split ring
models.formula: rA=(r cos theta,r sin theta); vA=(-omega r sin theta,omega r cos theta); B=(B,0); motional emf toward viewer at A proportional to -cos theta; eAB/Epk=-cos theta; brush voltage/Epk=abs(cos theta)
models.parameters: Dimensionless waveform, geometric drawing radius only; theta 0–360 degrees.
models.assumptions: Uniform field, fixed positive speed, ideal zero-width brushes, zero commutation time, negligible coil resistance. Distinct from radial-field averaged model.
checks: At theta=0: A emf into page, B out; positive left brush touches B.
At theta=180: coil emf reverses, positive left brush touches A.
At 90 and 270 degrees, emf is zero and contacts change.
Every brush emf value nonnegative.

models.title: Signed motor/generator model
models.formula: E=k*omega; I=(V-E)/R; T=k*I; Pin=V*I; Pconv=E*I; Pcu=I^2*R
models.parameters: V=120 V,R=.3 ohm,k=.25 V s/rad; omega=0–600 rad/s.
models.assumptions: Course ideal averaged machine; fixed field; no rotational, brush or excitation losses; reversible source.
checks: omega432 => I40 A,T10 Nm,Pin4800 W,Pconv4320 W,Pcu480 W.
omega480 => I0.
omega516 => I-30 A,T-7.5 Nm,Pin-3600 W,Pconv-3870 W,Pcu270 W.
Pin−Pconv=Pcu throughout speed range.

models.title: Excitation topology diagram
models.formula: Motor shunt It=Ia+If; series If=Ia; long shunt series field carries Ia; short shunt series field carries It.
models.assumptions: DC steady-state connectivity, resistances omitted visually in some field-topology drawings, field polarity not specified.
checks: Short-shunt top node after series coil.
Long-shunt field node before series coil.
Separate excitation has two electrically distinct loops.

models.title: Illustrative self-excitation intersection
models.formula: E(I,n)=(n/1000)*(3+120*tanh(1.4I)); equilibrium E=Rf*I, solved by bisection.
models.parameters: Rf60–230 ohm,n400–1200 rpm. 3V residual,120V amplitude,1.4/A saturation scale explicitly chosen for teaching.
models.assumptions: NOT measured data and NOT digitized course graph. Correct field polarity, no armature drop, steady state. Residual voltage makes high-R equilibrium small rather than identically zero.
checks: Residual emf E(0,1000)=3 V.
Positive slope decreases with positive I.
Equilibrium residual below1e-8 V.
Halving speed at fixed field current halves emf; self-excited field current generally changes.

models.title: Shunt power balance
models.formula: Motor: E=100−.1I,Pin=100(I+.99),Pout=EI−596.4. Generator: E=100+.1I,Pin=EI+603.6,Pout=100(I−1.01). Pcu=.1I²; Pfield=100If; eta=Pout/Pin.
models.parameters: I=6–120 A; k derived from99.4 V or100.6 V at1000 rpm.
models.assumptions: Fixed field and constant rotational losses; no brush or stray-load losses; field included in total machine boundary.
checks: Motor120A eta82.350607%; motor60A eta82.695524%.
Generator120A eta84.728987%; generator60A eta84.711931%.
Input−output−copper−field−rotational=0.

models.title: Torque-speed control
models.parameters: V60–120 V,f.6–1,Rs0–.9 ohm,T0–30 Nm; illustrative100 A limit.
models.assumptions: Fixed selected field, no rotational loss; constant-load torque.100 A is an illustrative teaching constraint, not a nameplate rating.
checks: Base V120,f1,Rs0,T10 => I40 A,omega432 rad/s.
At constant load, weakening field increases required current.
Points beyond100 A or negative speed are flagged.

models.title: Starting resistance
models.assumptions: Quasi-steady resistance-limited estimate, no time-domain simulation, no inferred inertia/inductance or resistor energy rating.
checks: For100 A limit Rs,min=.9 ohm.

examples.title: Single-loop starting, motor/generator and weakened field
examples.given: r.5m,l1m,B.25T,R.3ohm,V120V; torque10Nm opposing or7.5Nm driving; weakened B.2T.
examples.verification: Recomputed using k=2rlB, KVL and torque balance; separate energy balances4800=4320+480 and3870=3600+270. Assumed ideal radial-gap/averaged model.

examples.title: Generalized machine constant and increased driving torque
examples.verification: New steady Te=-10Nm, I=-40A. Mechanical input5280W=electrical output4800W+copper480W.

examples.title: Shunt-generator magnetization graph
examples.result: Maximum approx111V;Rfc20ohm;Rfcrit170ohm and addedcritical90ohm.55.5V at500rpm only under fixed-flux assumption. At fixedIf1A,50V corresponds500rpm, but field circuit needs50ohm total.
examples.source: C06-S01 pp30–31; independent physical check C06-S05
examples.verification: Graph readings explicitly approximate. Corrected fixed-flux versus self-excited distinction; no numeric self-excited half-speed answer invented.50ohm requirement incompatible with80ohm winding plus nonnegative series rheostat.

examples.title: Shunt motor losses and loading
examples.verification: Recomputed with full precision. Motor-output rating alone not used to infer120A. The source .4ohm half-load typo corrected to.1ohm; angular-speed unit corrected fromrpm torad/s.

examples.title: Shunt generator losses and loading
examples.verification: Corrected1200−100.6×6=603.6W. Reference condition not called no-load becauseIL=6−1.01=4.99A. Complete power balance checked.

examples.title: Armature voltage step
examples.verification: No premature rounding. Physical current continuity distinguished from zero-inductance fast estimate.

examples.title: Field weakening step
examples.verification: Torque constant ratio.8;steady I=40/.8;speed ratio195/(.8×200).Actual field also has a finite time constant.

examples.title: Added armature resistance
examples.verification: Full precision carried; source wording voltage reduced corrected to resistor inserted. Current continuity explicitly distinguished.

errata.issue: Angular-acceleration symbol and constant-torque work expression need explicit scope.
errata.resolution: Covered in Chapter5; alpha=domega/dt and W=integral(T dtheta), reducing toTtheta for constant torque.

errata.issue: Constant2rlB machine coefficient can be confused with an isolated coil rotating in uniform field.
errata.resolution: Example explicitly uses ideal radial-gap/averaged model. Uniform-field commutator visualization has its own angle-dependent model.

errata.issue: 55V after halving speed assumes unchanged flux, which is not generally true for fixed-resistance self-excitation.
errata.resolution: 55.5V presented only as fixed-flux estimate; exact self-excited result requires new curve intersection and is not asserted.

errata.issue: KeepingIf1A at50V requires50ohm, below the80ohm field winding resistance.
errata.resolution: 500rpm fixed-flux result is conditional on independent excitation or a changed field circuit.

errata.issue: Rated armature current120A is used by the worked solution although12kW output motor rating and100V do not alone establish that current.
errata.resolution: 120A treated as an explicit exercise convention.

errata.issue: Half-current line uses60×0.4 but states94V; correctRa is0.1ohm. Angular speed98.97 is labeledrpm.
errata.resolution: Use100−60×0.1=94V;speed945.67rpm or99.03rad/s. Use full precision for torque and efficiency.
Treat as reference operating point: external current4.99A, not no-load.
Correct rotational loss603.6W and propagate to loaded efficiency.

errata.issue: Instantaneous current calculation omits inductance; roundedbackemf causes avoidable current/speed discrepancies.
errata.resolution: Show finite-La currentcontinuity and separately fast electrical estimates with unchangedspeed; carry full precision.

errata.issue: Copied wording says voltage reduced although change is series resistance addition.
errata.resolution: State0.1ohm resistor insertion at unchanged110V supply.

coverage.coverage: Foundational force, emf, linear-machine dynamics, rotation and the original loop exercise are covered in Chapter5; essential equations reviewed in Chapter6.
